quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.body:
• Pick a monitor in the left panel, then drag across the centre grid to select cells.
• In the Apps tab, choose an app and click “Assign to Selection” to place it in those cells.
• Save the arrangement as a Layout (Layouts tab → + New Layout).
• Click Apply on a Layout to launch every app and tile it into place.

grid.title: The grid & assigning apps
grid.body:
• Drag across cells to select a rectangular region, then assign an app to it.
• Change a monitor's grid density with the Grid selector in the bottom bar (e.g. 6×6, 8×8, 10×10).
• Give a cell custom launch arguments in the Apps tab — for example a folder path for File Explorer — to open different windows of the same app.
• Clear Present Grid clears the current monitor; Clear All Grids clears every monitor (with a confirmation).

apps.title: Apps, URLs & Favorites
apps.body:
• Apps: pick from the built-in catalog, or click Browse… to add any program's .exe.
• URLs: build a group of browser tabs, choose a browser (+ Add Browser detects the browsers installed on your PC), and save it as a launchable item.
• Favorites: keep your most-used apps and URLs one click away.
• App History remembers programs you've added so you can reuse them later.

layouts.title: Layouts
layouts.body:
• A Layout stores which apps go where, across all your monitors.
• Apply launches and tiles everything; Edit reopens it on the grid; Export / Import share it as a .json file.
• If a saved app has no program or URL configured, that one app is skipped (with a warning) and the rest still save.

quickPresets.title: Quick Presets
quickPresets.body:
• A Quick Preset bundles several Layouts so you can apply them all together in one click.
• Create and manage them from “Manage QPs” in the left panel, then pick one and click Apply. Delete one from inside Manage QPs.
• Ctrl+Alt+1–9 applies Quick Presets A–I from anywhere, even when InstaDesk is not focused.
• Switch mode (the tick-box under Apply, off by default): with it on, applying a preset first CLOSES the windows of the preset currently in place, so you swap desks instead of stacking them. Nothing with unsaved work is forced — the app asks, and anything left open is listed by name.

snap.title: Snap
snap.body:
• Snap → M1 grabs the window you last used and snaps it into a region you choose — no Layout needed.
• A grid popup appears on the chosen monitor; click a region to place the window there.
• Some apps enforce their own position and may refuse to be moved.

monitorsSettings.title: Monitors & Settings
monitorsSettings.body:
• Use the Monitor selector to switch which display you're arranging; the Display Array shows how they're laid out.
• Settings lets you switch theme (Light / Dark / System), language (English / Español), the default grid size, and a bezel margin so tiled windows don't sit under your monitor frames.

troubleshooting.title: Tips & troubleshooting
troubleshooting.body:
• Some apps (certain CCTV / video tools) place their own windows and won't tile — close and relaunch them, or leave them out of the layout.
• Single-instance apps (e.g. Outlook, Teams) open just one window; assigning them to several cells won't create copies.
• Windows shortcuts (.lnk) can't be launched directly — point to the real .exe instead.
• If an app won't launch, check its path in the Apps tab and use Browse… to fix it.

urlsFavorites.title: URLs & Favorites
urlsFavorites.body:
A URL group is a browser window described by its tabs — not a bookmark list. Build one in Apps → URLs: pick the browser, add a tab group, list the addresses, then Save. It becomes an entry you can assign to a region exactly like a program.

Open behaviour decides the shape: one window for everything, one window per group, or a separate window per address when each needs its own region.

Favorites are simply pinned apps — the four or five you place in almost every Layout, kept one click away instead of a search.

To change a group later, open Apps → Apps, press Edit at the top of the list, then Edit on the group itself. The builder reopens with its addresses already in place, so you change the one you meant instead of retyping the rest. The name stays fixed while editing, because saved Layouts refer to a group by its name.

monitor-select.title: Start by choosing a screen
monitor-select.body: InstaDesk arranges one monitor at a time. Pick the screen you want to lay out here — everything below applies to whichever one is selected.

grid-size-picker.title: Decide how finely to divide it
grid-size-picker.body: This splits the chosen screen into a grid. 4×4 gives you sixteen sizeable regions; 10×10 lets you place things very precisely. You can change it per monitor, at any time.

workspace-grid.title: Pick the region an app should fill
workspace-grid.body: This is your chosen screen, drawn as that grid. Drag across cells to select a region — one cell for a narrow panel, a block of them for a wide window.

assign-buttons.title: Put an app in the region
assign-buttons.body: With a region selected, choose an app from the list and press Assign to Selection. That is the whole idea: this app, that space, on this screen.

layout-new-button.title: Save the arrangement as a Layout
layout-new-button.body: Once the grid holds the apps you want, save it. A Layout remembers every app and the exact region it belongs in, across all your monitors.

qp-apply-button.title: And this is what it buys you
qp-apply-button.body: Press Apply and every app in the Layout opens and lands in its saved region, across every screen, in one click. That is the point of all of the above.

grid-size-picker.title: How finely the screen is divided
grid-size-picker.body: Each monitor has its own grid size — 4×4, 6×6, 8×8 or 10×10. A wide monitor suits a finer grid; 4×4 is easier to work with on a small screen. Changing it clears that monitor’s current cells — your saved Layouts are untouched.

workspace-grid.title: Selecting a region
workspace-grid.body: Click a cell, or drag across several, to select the region a window should fill. Ctrl-click adds a separate region to the selection.

grid-status.title: What is selected right now
grid-status.body: This line always tells you how many cells are selected and how many already hold an app.

clear-current-button.title: Starting this screen over
clear-current-button.body: Clear Present Grid empties the monitor you are looking at. The others are left alone.

clear-all-grids-button.title: Starting everything over
clear-all-grids-button.body: Clear All Grids wipes every monitor at once, so it asks you to confirm first. Again: saved Layouts and Quick Presets are not affected.

tab-apps.title: Where apps come from
tab-apps.body: The Apps tab is where you pick what goes into the region you have selected.

apps-subtabs.title: Three kinds of thing
apps-subtabs.body: Apps is your installed programs. Favorites is the shortlist you use constantly. URLs builds a set of browser tabs that open together as one window.

assign-buttons.title: Assigning and unassigning
assign-buttons.body: Select a region, pick an app, then Assign to Selection. Unassign Selection empties the region again without touching anything else.

apps-launch-args-hint.title: Two windows of the same app
apps-launch-args-hint.body: Select cells and a "Launch args" box appears here. Give two regions of the SAME app different values — typically a different folder — and you get two windows. Identical values mean one. (Outlook and Teams only ever run one window, whatever you set.)

tab-layouts.title: Saved arrangements
tab-layouts.body: A Layout is a whole desk in one file — every app, its region, on every monitor.

layout-new-button.title: Saving what you built
layout-new-button.body: New Layout captures the current grids exactly as they stand. It stays greyed out until at least one app has been assigned, so there is something to save.

layouts-list.title: Your saved Layouts
layouts-list.body: Every Layout you have saved appears here, newest work at the top.

layout-show-content.title: Seeing inside one
layout-show-content.body: Show content draws the Layout as a diagram — the same picture the walkthrough uses — so you can check what is in it before applying it.

layout-card-actions.title: Apply, Edit, Export, Delete
layout-card-actions.body: Apply opens everything and places it. Edit loads it back into the grid so you can change it. Export writes it to a file you can keep or move to another machine. Delete removes the Layout itself — the apps inside it are untouched, and it cannot be undone.

layout-import-button.title: Bringing one in
layout-import-button.body: Import reads a Layout file back — the other half of Export, for moving between machines.

layout-capture-button.title: Capture what you already have
layout-capture-button.body: Capture current layout turns your desktop, as it stands, into a Layout. It is also the only way to record a multi-window app — one program that opens several windows. Those can’t be drawn in the grid, so an edited Layout looks emptier than it is, but they are kept when you save.

quick-presets-section.title: Several Layouts, one click
quick-presets-section.body: A Quick Preset bundles Layouts together. Where a Layout sets up one screen, a Quick Preset can set up your whole desk for a particular kind of work.

qp-manage-button.title: Building one
qp-manage-button.body: Manage QPs is where you create a bundle, name it, and choose which Layouts belong in it. It is also where you delete one: deleting a Quick Preset never removes the Layouts inside it.

qp-dropdown.title: Choosing what to run
qp-dropdown.body: This lists your Quick Presets and your individual Layouts together — pick either.

qp-apply-button.title: Running it
qp-apply-button.body: Apply launches everything in the bundle and places each window on the screen it belongs to. On its own it only ever ADDS to what is already open. You can also apply Quick Presets A–I from anywhere with Ctrl+Alt+1 to 9, even when InstaDesk is not the focused window.

qp-switch-mode.title: Switch mode — one preset at a time
qp-switch-mode.body: Leave this off and Apply behaves as above. Turn it on and Apply first CLOSES the windows of the preset currently in place, so you swap desks instead of stacking them. Anything with unsaved work is asked politely and never forced, and whatever stays open is listed for you by name.

apps-subtabs.title: Two more ways to fill a region
apps-subtabs.body: Besides installed programs, a region can hold a set of browser tabs (URLs) or an app you pinned for quick reach (Favorites). Both end up in the same place: assigned to a region.

urls-builder.title: A URL group is a browser window
urls-builder.body: Pick the browser, then build the window you want. This is not a bookmark list — it is a description of one window and the tabs that should open inside it.

urls-add-tab-group.title: One group, one window
urls-add-tab-group.body: Each tab group becomes its own browser window, with every URL in it opening as a tab. Add a second group when you want two separate windows — say, research on one screen and dashboards on another.

urls-open-behavior.title: How they open
urls-open-behavior.body: One window puts every tab together. One per group gives each group its own window. One per URL opens every address in a window of its own — useful when each needs a region.

urls-save.title: Save, then assign it like an app
urls-save.body: Saving turns the set into an entry you can pick from the Apps list and assign to a region, exactly like a program. That is the point: a browser window becomes something a Layout can place.

favorites-add.title: Favorites are a shortlist
favorites-add.body: Add favorite pins an app so it is one click away instead of a search. It changes nothing about how the app behaves — only how quickly you can reach it here.

favorites-list.title: Your pinned apps
favorites-list.body: Favorites appear here and in the Apps list. Worth pinning the four or five you place in almost every Layout.

snap-button.title: Snap — for one window, right now
snap-button.body: Snap is the quick one. Press it, drag a rectangle over the screen, and the window you last used jumps into that space. No Layout, no saving — just this window, there.

minimize-all-button.title: Clearing the desk, temporarily
minimize-all-button.body: Minimize all drops every window out of the way. Press it again and each one returns to the exact region it was in — not merely un-minimised, but back where it belongs.

close-all-button.title: Clearing the desk, properly
close-all-button.body: Close all windows asks every window to close gracefully, so anything with unsaved work still prompts you first. InstaDesk itself stays open. It always confirms before running.

bottom-status.title: What just happened
bottom-status.body: Results appear here — how many windows moved, and anything that was skipped.

monitor-select.title: Which screen you are arranging
monitor-select.body: Everything in the centre grid applies to the monitor chosen here.

display-array.title: How Windows sees your screens
display-array.body: This is the physical arrangement — which monitor sits where. It mirrors what Windows reports, so if a screen is in the wrong place here, it is in the wrong place there too.

identify-monitors-button.title: Which one is Monitor 2?
identify-monitors-button.body: Identify monitors flashes a large number onto every physical screen, so you can match the numbers above to the displays actually on your desk.

settings-default-grid.title: The grid size new monitors get
settings-default-grid.body: Monitors you have not set individually use this default.

settings-window-margin.title: Leaving room at the edges
settings-window-margin.body: Window margin insets tiled windows slightly, which helps if your monitor bezels or a taskbar would otherwise clip a window edge.

settings-theme.title: Light or dark
settings-theme.body: Theme follows Windows by default; set it explicitly here if you would rather it did not.

settings-check-updates.title: How new versions arrive
settings-check-updates.body: InstaDesk checks for signed updates and tells you when one is available — you decide when to install it. You can also check here whenever you like. Updates are signed, so the app will refuse anything that has been tampered with.

settings-list.title: The settings worth knowing about
settings-list.body: Three that are easy to miss: Launch on system start puts InstaDesk in your Windows start-up; the telemetry switch turns anonymous usage reporting off entirely; and License shows your trial or licence state and lets you enter a key.

version-status.title: Is the engine running?
version-status.body: The dot is green and the label reads “live” when the background component that actually moves your windows is running. If it is amber or red, layouts will not apply — that is the first thing to check.

bottom-status.title: Windows that refuse to move
bottom-status.body: A few programs reposition themselves after being placed, and some run as administrator and cannot be touched at all. When that happens it is reported here rather than failing silently.

help-open-manual.title: The full manual
help-open-manual.body: The complete manual opens as a PDF in your language, for anything this walkthrough does not cover.
